::: {.lede}
A 0.8B model, trained only on a 2B model's answers, calls tools better than the 2B does. Three ways
of distilling end in a tie; what separates them is cost, and tools they have never seen.
:::

## The question

[Outline: distillation is what you do with queries but no answers, and a better model than the one
you want to ship. The task (xLAM-60k), the pair (Qwen3.5-2B → 0.8B, ADR 0004), the budget (one
RTX 3060), and the question: how close does a label-free student get to one trained on gold labels?]{.outline-only}

## The data

[Outline: what a task looks like (query, offered tools, gold calls); the grouped split (ADR 0001);
the label audit and `test-clean` (ADR 0002, 0005); gold's habit of writing defaults.]{.outline-only}

## Measuring it

[Outline: strict and lenient exact match, no LLM judge; BFCL for tools never seen in training; paired
McNemar tests with Holm across every claim (ADR 0009).]{.outline-only}

## What we found

[Outline: the label-free tie and why B is the headline; "faster, not better" on unseen tools; the
student beats its teacher, and it isn't format; imitation vs accuracy; serving cost.]{.outline-only}
